finding.claim: For negative numbers argument.toString(16/2/8) includes a leading '-', so '0x'+hex yields '0x-...' (and '0b-...', '0o-...') which is a SyntaxError instead of '-0x...'; fractional and non-finite values also yield invalid literals like '0x1.8' or '0xNAN'.
finding.title: Hexadecimal/binary/octal formatting produces invalid literals for negative and non-integer numbers

verifier.reason: The code at jsesc.js:216-226 unconditionally builds '0x' + argument.toString(16), '0b' + argument.toString(2), and '0o' + argument.toString(8) with no sign, fractional, or non-finite handling, so negative values produce '0x-ff'-style invalid literals and fractional/non-finite values produce '0x1.8'/'0xNAN'-style invalid literals before returning at jsesc.js:228-231.
